properties.areaDesc: Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 26 at 3:35PM PST until November 29 at 5:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, An increased risk for
sneaker waves and strong rip currents with breaking waves of 13
to 19 feet. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 1.7 ft of
inundation above ground level is possible in low- lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Bayside locations along southern Monterey Bay including
Elkhorn Slough.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Friday
evening. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 5 PM PST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning,
pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.7 ft above normal (7.5 ft MLLW) at 12:31 PM
Friday, 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 1:28 PM Saturday,
and 0.9 ft above normal (6.8 ft MLLW) at 2:32 PM Sunday. These
predictions include up to 1.3 ft of surge that will enhance the
astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90
minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the
San Francisco Bay, respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Stay off of jetties, piers, rocks, and other waterside
infrastructure. Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf
and NEVER turn your back on the ocean. Monitor local weather,
surf and tide forecasts at www.weather.gov/mtr.

properties.areaDesc: Northern Coastal Humboldt
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 26 at 2:54PM PST until November 27 at 3:00PM PST by NWS Eureka CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...High astronomical tides will cause minor flooding in low
lying areas around Humboldt Bay. Up to one half foot of
saltwater inundation above ground level is possible near
shorelines and tidal waterways. Between 9.0 and 9.4 feet MLLW
at the North Spit tide gauge is predicted.

* WHERE...Northern Coastal Humboldt County.

* WHEN...From 11 AM to 3 PM PST Friday. High tide is at 12:48 PM at
the Humboldt Bay North Spit tide gauge. Saltwater inundation
will be possible 1 to 2 hours before and after high tide.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of low lying areas around Humboldt Bay
including parks and roads with only isolated closures
expected. Flooding will likely impact Jackson Ranch Road in
the Arcata Bottoms and several roads in King Salmon.
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory indicates that onshore winds and tides
will combine to generate flooding of low areas along the shore.

Feet Above Ground is locally defined as feet above the Highest
Astronomical Tide or HAT.

properties.areaDesc: San Luis Obispo County Beaches; Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 26 at 1:15PM PST until November 27 at 3:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 10 to 15
feet with dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 3 PM PST Friday.
For the High Surf Advisory, until 3 PM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths,
and harbor walkways. Moderate beach erosion is likely.
Isolated damage is unlikely but possible. There is an
increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull
swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can
cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize
small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...An abnormally high tide of around 7.4
feet will peak near 11 AM Friday morning.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do
NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.areaDesc: Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 26 at 1:15PM PST until November 26 at 9:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 6 to 10
feet with dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until noon PST Friday.
For the High Surf Advisory, until 9 PM PST this evening.

* IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths,
and harbor walkways. Moderate beach erosion is likely.
Isolated damage is unlikely but possible. There is an
increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull
swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can
cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize
small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...An abnormally high tide of around 7.7
feet will peak just after 10 AM Friday morning.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do
NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued November 26 at 12:15PM PST until November 27 at 1:00PM PST by NWS San Diego CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Significant coastal flooding expected.

* WHERE...Orange County Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...Through 1 PM PST Friday. Most susceptible time of
flooding will during the morning high tide, with peak tides
trending occurring once again late Friday morning.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...King tides peaked this morning just under 8
feet. A long period west swell will bring high surf today, and
breaking waves may reach 6-9 feet with local sets up to 10 feet
on west-facing beaches. Surf lowers to 3-6 feet by Friday
morning's high tide..
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.
